#en: This patch of orbit looks harmless at a glance, just another empty lane ships cut through on their way to more important places, and that is exactly why it works. When a system gets logged as safe often enough, pilots stop checking the numbers, supervisors stop re-running the stress models, and anything slipped into that blind spot can run for years without a second look. If Torque has been testing how far he can push grav fields before they scream, it would be out here, where routine bred laziness. So far I have a blurred chain: a half-forgotten surface log about anomalous spin, an unregistered cache adrift where no one should have built anything, and a growing list of ships with drive readings that do not match their flight histories, all pointing toward someone quietly using our habits against us.
zh: 这片轨道乍看人畜无害，不过是船只在前往更要紧之地途中切过的又一条空航道——而这正是它奏效的原因。当一个系统被足够频繁地登记为安全，飞行员就不再核对数字，主管就不再重跑应力模型，而溜进那个盲点的任何东西都能运行多年而无人再看第二眼。如果"扭矩"一直在测试引力场在被逼到尖叫之前能推多远，那就会是在这里，在这种例行公事养出惰性之处。目前为止，我有一条模糊的链条：一份关于异常自旋的半遗忘地面日志、一处漂在没人该建任何东西之处的未登记储藏点，以及一份越来越长的、引擎读数与飞行史不符的船只清单——全都指向有人在悄悄利用我们的习惯对付我们。

#en: Out here, pinned in quiet orbit above anonymous cloud and rock, is the one place his adjustments can be seen without all the planetary noise. Away from port auditors and Harmonization filters, the traffic offsets he sold to pirates and nervous captains resolve into clean geometry, revealing which windows were genuine rescues and which were sharpened into blades. Whoever helped him build this layer of the scheme made sure no one on the ground had to say its name; the absence in every report is almost louder than the data. So far, the trail runs through a forgotten dataslate, a compromised courier, and a scrubbed Navy patrol, then down into the under-levels of New Atlantis where his habits began; each step tightening the circle around a man who moves ships by leaving all the most important words unsaid.
zh: 在这里，钉在无名云层与岩石上方的安静轨道中，是他那些调整唯一能在没有全部行星噪声的情况下被看到的地方。远离港口审计员与"协调过滤器"，他卖给海盗与紧张船长的交通偏移解析成干净的几何，揭示哪些窗口是真正的救援、哪些被磨成了刀刃。帮他搭起这一层方案的人确保了地面上没人需要说出它的名字；每一份报告里的那种缺席，几乎比数据本身更响。目前为止，这条线索穿过一块被遗忘的数据板、一艘被攻陷的信使船，以及一支被擦净的海军巡逻队，再向下钻进新亚特兰蒂斯城的下层——他的习惯正是从那里开始的；每一步都收紧着围绕一个人的圆圈——他靠把最重要的那些词全部略去来移动船只。

#en: Out here, in a base the UC forgot even before the paint peeled, the wrong kind of tech can sit unnoticed for years, passed from one petty outfit to the next until it becomes part of the scenery. The Razor Strays are not guarding this place for nostalgia; they are guarding something they barely understand, inherited from some old officer who never filed the right shut-down order. Left alone, it will keep seeding the lanes with bad math and worse ideas for anyone willing to pay. So far the trail has been a stack of small mistakes a corrupted slate on a lonely rock, a "clerical error" in a Trade Authority hold, half-sanitized sims in a bunker like this each one an oversight someone thought they would fix later, each one another step in the path of a navigator who learned how to turn neglect into a weapon.
zh: 在这里、在一座联殖在油漆剥落之前就已遗忘的基地里，那种"错误的"技术能多年无人注意地坐着，被从一支小队伍传给下一支，直到成为风景的一部分。剃刀流浪帮守在这里不是为了怀旧；他们守着一件自己几乎不理解的东西，是从某个从未提交正确关停令的老军官那里继承来的。任其自生自灭，它会继续为任何愿意付钱的人在航道里播下坏数学与更坏的点子。目前为止，这条线索是一摞小错误：孤独岩石上一块损坏的数据板、贸易管理局货舱里的一处"文书记录错误"、像这样一座掩体里半清理过的模拟——每一处都是有人以为以后再修的疏忽，每一处都是那名学会把忽视变成武器的领航员路径上的又一步。

#en: Down here the ceilings sweat and the walls carry every rumor; this is where routes get rewritten for credits, and where someone like him would hide a key inside ordinary traffic. In the Well, shiphands, off-duty LIST clerks, and GalBank debtors all move through the same narrow corridors, their secrets pressed close, their voices kept low so no analyst up top can triangulate loose talk. Whatever pattern he left pointing toward that hidden homestead would have to pass through a place like this, disguised as a scrap of nav code or a forgotten contract, buried where only those already drowning in numbers would dare to look. So far the trail runs from a stray dataslate in the black, to corrupted orbitals, to whispered mentions of failed basins and a pilot who keeps turning safe worlds into statistical ghosts.
zh: 在这下面，天花板在渗水，墙壁承载着每一则传闻；这里是航线为信用币被改写的地方，也是像他那样的人会把一把钥匙藏进寻常交通里的地方。在深井区，船工、休班的独立盟文书与盖尔银行欠债人都在同样的狭窄走廊里移动，他们的秘密贴身藏紧，把声音压低，好让上面任何分析员都无法三角定位闲话。他留下来指向那座隐藏农庄的任何模式，都必然要经过这样的地方，伪装成一小段导航代码或一份被遗忘的合同，埋在那里——只有那些已经淹死在数字里的人敢去看。目前为止，线索从漆黑中一块散落数据板，到损坏的轨道数据，再到关于失败盆地与一名不断把安全世界变成统计幽灵的飞行员那些低语的提及。

#en: The trail starts in this quiet research module because this is where someone first tried to erase the lines she drew and failed. The stolen routing work that passed through these servers did not vanish, it smeared its fingerprints across cached telemetry, half-scrubbed backups, and error logs no one bothered to purge. If she hijacked a data-theft chain here, then the patterns she was hiding from and the ones she was creating both brushed the same systems, leaving just enough residue for someone patient to reconstruct a direction of travel. So far all I know is that analysts saw impossible approach curves in their feeds, then someone upstream ordered a cleanup, and the only reason any of it still exists is that past edits were lazy, leaving faint echoes of corridors that should not intersect where they do.
zh: 线索从这座安静的研究舱开始，是因为这里正是有人第一次试图抹掉她画下的线条却失败的地方。流经这些服务器的被盗航线工程并未消失，它的指纹抹在缓存的遥测、半擦除的备份，以及没人费心清除的错误日志上。若她在这里劫持了一条数据盗窃链，那么她躲开的模式与她创造的模式都擦过同一批系统，留下刚好足够的残迹，让有耐心的人重建出一个行进方向。目前为止我只知道，分析员在他们的数据流里看到了不可能的进近曲线，然后上游有人下令清理，而这一切还存在的唯一原因，是过去的编辑太懒，留下了那些本不该在彼处相交的走廊的淡淡回声。

#en: Cydonia's fringe is where the city's light thins and the dust takes over, a no-man's land of dead loaders, rusting refinery towers, and forgotten survey shacks humming with old UC telemetry. Out here Vector can splice herself into the traffic grid without too many eyes noticing when a lane bends the wrong way, and she has ringed the outskirts with portable beacons tuned to scramble every approach that relies on sanctioned charts. If she hard-burns her private atlas through those rigs, the Settled Systems inherit her routes without her, and nobody will ever agree whether that is justice or convenience. From the buried slate on that remote rock to the redacted files in New Atlantis and the orbital clue pried from an Ecliptic screen, every line has curved toward this pilot rewriting the map in her own image.
zh: 赛多尼亚的边缘，是城市灯光变稀薄、尘土接管一切的地方，一片由死掉的装载机、生锈的炼油塔，以及嗡鸣着旧联殖遥测的被遗忘勘探棚构成的无主之地。"向量"能在这里把自己接进交通网格，而不会在一条航道弯错方向时被太多眼睛注意到；她还在外围环布了便携信标，调校来扰乱每一次依赖获批星图的进近。若她通过那些设备把自己的私人地图硬烧出去，定居星系就会在没有她的情况下继承她的航线，而永远没人会就"那是正义还是便利"达成一致。从那块遥远岩石上被埋的数据板，到新亚特兰蒂斯城里的涂黑文件，再到从黄道佣兵团屏幕上撬出的轨道线索，每一条线都弯向这名按自己的模样改写星图的飞行员。

#en:
Gagarin Landing is all scaffolds and secondhand promises, a place where yesterday's industry was gutted and today's work happens in back rooms no one audits.  
If any station in the Settled Systems would quietly trial hardware built from skewed data, it would be this one, with its mix of desperate locals and cost-cutting offworld executives.  
Somewhere in these refurbished bays is the piece that proves Vector's math is not just theory, a system tuned to the same crooked pattern that keeps surfacing in wreck telemetry.  
So far all I have are fragments and ghost paperwork; a nameless slate from a forgotten outpost, misaligned jump traces off a crippled freighter, and a half-redacted log from an isolated agent, all pointing to ships dying the same strange way without a single clean record explaining why.
zh:
加加林着陆点满是脚手架与二手承诺，一个昨日工业被掏空、今日工作发生在无人审计的后室的地方。  
若说定居星系里有哪座星际站会悄悄试用由扭曲数据造出的硬件，那就是这一座——它混杂着绝望的当地人与削减成本的太空高管。  
在这些翻新的货舱里某处，是那件证明"向量"的数学不只是理论的零件：一套调校到与残骸遥测中不断浮现的同样歪斜模式的系统。  
目前为止，我只有碎片与幽灵文书：一块来自被遗忘前哨的无名数据板、一艘残废货船上错位的跃迁痕迹，以及一名孤立特工半涂黑的日志，全都指向船只以同样古怪的方式死去，却没有一份干净的记录解释原因。

#en: This lonely orbit has been a dumping ground for deferred problems for years, a quiet holding pattern where old refuel nodes, dead beacons, and forgotten contracts drift until someone remembers to clean the slate. That habit of leaving things circling, unresolved, made it the perfect anchor for a navigation construct designed to outlast memories and overwrite patrol charts in slow, invisible increments. Left intact, it keeps bending ships along the same narrow band of space, feeding Vector the predictable traffic she needs to stay ahead of every pursuit. Earlier, a stray dataslate in the black mentioned altered routes, and a gutted freighter's logs confirmed impossible course corrections; now, this orbital clue is where those stories start to intersect, pointing to a single hand quietly reshaping the lanes.
zh: 这条孤独的轨道多年来一直是延期问题的倾倒场，一个安静的滞留区——旧的补给节点、死掉的信标与被遗忘的合同在此漂着，直到有人想起要来清账。那种把东西留在轨道上、悬而不决的习惯，使它成了一座导航构造物的完美锚点；那座构造物设计来比记忆活得更久，并以缓慢、看不见的增量覆写巡逻星图。任其完好，它会继续把船只沿同一条狭窄的太空带掰弯，为"向量"提供她保持在每一次追击之前所需的可预测交通。早先，漆黑中一块散落数据板提到被改动的航线，一艘被掏空货船的日志证实了不可能的航向修正；如今，这个轨道线索正是那些故事开始交汇之处，指向一只悄悄重塑航道的单只手。

#en: The fragment of shattered drive housing drifts where no one ever meant it to matter, spinning lazily in a thin ring of junked metal and dead satellites; yet the telemetry echoing from its scorched casing ties together pressure lines, ship routes, and storm signatures that keep repeating in your files. Whatever calibration was once done here has been reused, repurposed, nudged a little further each time until this forgotten orbit became a quiet hinge between smugglers, old UC hardware, and an engineer who prefers to stand nowhere she was officially assigned. So far you have followed a trail from a lonely outpost in the dust, to a dead hunter's battered ship, to freight records in a rusting factory town and altered harvests on the frontier, each step shifting the pattern closer to this unseen axis in the sky.
zh: 那块碎裂的引擎外壳残片漂在没人曾想过它会要紧的地方，懒洋洋地旋转在一圈废旧金属与死卫星构成的细环里；可从它烧焦外壳中回荡出的遥测，却把不断在你的文件里重复的压力线、船只航线与风暴签名串在一起。这里曾经做过的无论什么校准都被重复利用、改作他用、每次都再推远一点，直到这条被遗忘的轨道成了走私者、旧联殖硬件，以及一名偏爱站在任何官方未曾指派给她之处的工程师之间一个安静的铰链。目前为止，你追着线索从尘土中一座孤独前哨，到一艘死掉猎人的破船，到一座锈蚀工厂镇的货运记录与边境上被改动的收成，每一步都把模式推得更靠近天空中这条看不见的轴。

#en: A husk like the FC-9470 Prairiefire is where bad habits go to calcify; a bounty cutter once meant for clean contracts and short-term holds, now adrift with its databanks still humming, auto-archiving side deals no one bothered to erase when the lights went out. If brokers were quietly hiring someone to bend storms around smuggling routes, this is where the first retainers would have been filed, a "temporary" workaround that became standard practice with every unreported payout. Strip those records out here and the pattern of who bought favorable weather, and where they needed it most, will finally start to show. Up to this point the trail has been fragments: a lonely stash in the dust, a wrecked hunter's half-burned log, and a frontier manifest full of shipments that somehow always sailed between the storms.
zh: 像"FC-9470 草原之火"这样的空壳，是坏习惯钙化之处；一艘赏金切割船，当初本是为干净合同与短期羁押而造，如今漂着，数据库仍在嗡鸣，自动归档着灯光熄灭时没人费心抹掉的私下交易。若掮客在悄悄雇人把风暴掰绕走私航线，这里就是最早的那批聘约被归档的地方，一种"临时"变通，随着每一笔未申报的付款变成了标准做法。在这里把这些记录剥出来，谁买了顺风天气、又最需要在哪里，这个模式终于会开始显形。到目前为止，这条线索都是碎片：尘土中一处孤独的藏匿点、一名失事猎人半烧毁的日志，以及一份满是"不知怎地总能在风暴之间航行"的货运的边境舱单。

#en: On this little cargo module clinging to a dead moon, ships only stop long enough to shed weight and disappear from questions, which makes it the one place where a nervous broker could hide records that never should have existed. The station hums with old generators and half-paid docking fees, a perfect limbo for manifests that list ships twice, captains who deny ever owning them, and routes that dead-end in empty space. Here, in the gaps between official ledgers, the pattern of a quiet auditor's hand might still be pieced together, if the fragments have not already been scrubbed. So far the trail is only a broken complaint slate from an abandoned shack and hangar gossip about underpriced hulls changing names too often, more rumor than record, with nothing yet that explains how the first ship was really taken.
zh: 在这座攀附在死卫星上的小货运舱里，船只只停留到刚好卸下重量、并从问询中消失，这让它成了某个紧张掮客唯一能藏起本不该存在之记录的地方。这座星际站因老旧发电机与付了一半的停泊费而嗡鸣，是舱单把船只列两次、船长否认曾拥有它们、航线在空荡太空中断头的完美悬置地。在这里、在官方账册之间的空隙里，一名安静审计员的手笔也许仍能被拼出来——如果那些碎片还没被擦掉。目前为止，这条线索只有一块来自废弃棚屋的损坏投诉数据板，以及机库闲话关于低价船壳换名太频的议论；传闻多于记录，还没有任何东西能解释第一艘船究竟是如何被拿走的。

#en: The signal only exists out here, in the thin static between worn orbital paths where no registry admits anything was ever parked. Whatever is broadcasting rides the same curve as old medical transports and unscheduled evac flights, too regular to be random, too quiet to be honest, as if some forgotten routing order is still echoing long after the war that birthed it was filed away. Scans disagree on how many relays are in the chain, timestamps smear across different campaigns, and every recovered log looks like it has been rewritten at least once by an uncredited hand.  \nSo far all we can pin down are fragments: a nameless cache on a backworld, a dead hulk whispering scrambled commands, a gutted UC frame with its history carved out, each pointing toward a medic who has never truly stepped off the triage line.
zh: 那道信号只存在于这里，存在于老旧轨道路径之间稀薄的静电里——任何登记册都不承认那里曾停放过任何东西。正在广播的东西与旧医疗运输船和未排期的撤离飞行走着同一条曲线，太规律不像随机，太安静不像诚实，仿佛某道被遗忘的航线路由命令在那场催生它的战争被归档很久之后仍在回响。扫描结果对这条链里有几座中继说法不一，时戳在不同战役之间糊成一片，而每一份被找回的日志都像是至少被一只未署名的手改写过一次。  \n目前为止我们能钉住的只有碎片：一穷乡星上一处无名储藏点、一具低声说着错乱指令的死残骸、一具历史被剜掉的被掏空联殖船架，每一处都指向一名从未真正走下分诊线的医疗兵。

#en: Neon Starport is the only place she could choose to finish this, a tangle of launch lanes and grav beacons where every route out of the city narrows to a handful of controlled vectors. Here, under the noise of freight traffic and tourist liners, she can hide one decisive burn inside the churn of a hundred departures, then vanish into the same anomaly that stole her squadron. UC watchers, Freestar eyes, and corporate ghosts all crowd the manifests, each waiting to see whether she escapes with what her implants remember or dies with those seconds still locked inside her skull. From a quiet corporate office you trailed erased flight plans and Ryujin drift data, then out in dead Vanguard metal you found proof that something was cut from the record; every line, every rumor, has bent you inexorably toward this dock.
zh: 霓虹城太空港是她唯一可能选择来完成此事的地方——一片由发射航道与引力信标构成的乱麻，城市每一条出港路线都收窄成少数几条受控向量。在这里，在货运交通与观光邮轮的噪声之下，她能把一次决定性的燃烧藏进上百次离港的搅动里，然后消失进那个夺走她中队的同一异常。联殖监视者、自由星系联盟的眼线，以及公司的幽灵全都挤在舱单里，各自等着看她究竟是带着她植入体记得的东西逃脱，还是带着那几秒仍锁在颅骨里死去。从一间安静的公司办公室起，你追过被抹除的飞行计划与龙神的漂移数据，然后在死掉的先锋队金属里你找到"记录中有东西被剪掉"的证据；每一条线、每一则传闻，都不可阻挡地把你推向这个船坞。

#en: Out here, the outpost sits half-forgotten above a nameless rock, humming just loud enough to pass for routine. If Torque cached the first drafts of his collapse doctrine anywhere, it would be in a place everyone thinks they already understand, where old logs roll by unchecked and no one bothers to ask why the stress models do not match the traffic. The techs who pass through argue in low voices about whether that waste ring failure years back was bad luck, bad metal, or something worse, but the talk always trails off when someone important walks in. So far I have a patchwork: a single remote station that recorded anomalous spin, a drifting cache in empty orbit crammed with tampered drive data, and a trail of "accidents" whose reports all disagree on the details but point, quietly, toward the same careful hand.
zh: 在这里，那座前哨半被遗忘地坐落在一颗无名岩石上方，嗡鸣得刚好够冒充例行公事。如果"扭矩"把他的坍缩学说最初草稿缓存在任何地方，那就会在一个所有人都以为自己已经了解的地方——旧日志不受检查地滚过，没人费心问为什么应力模型与交通对不上。路过的技师低声争论多年前那次废料环故障是霉运、坏金属、还是更糟的东西，可只要有大人物走进来，谈话总会散掉。目前为止，我有一块拼凑：一座记录了异常自旋的单独远程星际站、一处塞满被篡改引擎数据的空轨漂移储藏点，以及一连串"事故"——它们的报告在细节上全不一致，却都悄悄指向同一只谨慎的手。

#en: The Den is exactly the sort of place people forget about until they need something left off the books. UC colors on the bulkheads, Vanguard uniforms in the corridors, and a station assignment nobody fights for because nothing ever happens in this system, officially. That makes it perfect for burying the kind of paperwork that turns derelicts into ghosts and missing crews into accounting entries. Whatever someone locked away here was meant to sleep under layers of routine inspections and disinterest.  \n\nSo far it has been a string of accidents that felt like luck: a misfiled cache on a backworld rock, an offhand comment in a quiet bar, a pattern in drift data that did not match its story. One coincidence is chance. Three start to look like intent, all pointing toward a salvager who only exists in the margins.
zh: 巢穴站正是那种人们会忘记、直到他们需要某样不走账册的东西时才想起的地方。舱壁上是联殖的颜色，走廊里是先锋队的制服，还有一份没人争抢的星际站指派——因为按官方说法，这个星系从不出事。这让它成了埋葬那种"把弃船变成幽灵、把失踪船员变成会计条目"的文书的完美之地。有人锁在这里的任何东西，本都该在层层例行检查与漠不关心之下沉睡。  \n\n目前为止，它是一连串感觉像运气的意外：穷乡岩石上一处归档错误的储藏点、一家安静酒吧里的一句随口之言、一段与自身说法不符的漂移数据模式。一次巧合是偶然。三次就开始像有意为之，全都指向一名只存在于页边的打捞者。

#en: Down here, beneath Neon's gloss, the air tastes of metal and spilled Aurora, and every cable-strung corridor feels like part of a nervous system somebody rewired in a hurry. This is where off-the-books processors move through gloved hands, where nav code and storm data can be traded like street chems, and where a cautious engineer could hide the blueprint for disappearing between sensor gaps. If there is a pattern that can point the way to him, it lives in these jury-rigged stacks and smuggled thoughtware, not in any clean corporate tower. Out on that forgotten rock the first rumor surfaced; at the abandoned station, recordings cut off mid-sentence; by the time the stories reached the shadows of Neon, every retelling bent the same direction, as if the whole trail had always been sliding toward this underbelly.
zh: 在这下面、在霓虹城的亮面之下，空气尝起来有金属与洒出的极光味，每一条挂满线缆的走廊都像某个被人匆忙重接过神经系统的部位。这里正是账外处理器在戴手套的手之间流转、导航代码与风暴数据能像街头毒品一样被交易、一名谨慎工程师能藏起"在传感器空隙间消失"之蓝图的地方。若说有什么模式能指向他，它就活在这些勉强拼凑的机架与走私来的思维硬件里，而不在任何干净的公司塔楼里。在那块被遗忘的岩石上，第一则传闻浮出水面；在那座废弃星际站，录音在句子中间中断；等故事传到霓虹城的阴影里时，每一次重述都朝同一方向弯曲，仿佛整条线索一直滑向这个下腹。

#en: This forgotten Deimos scrapyard is where every missing shipment, every ghost-hauler rumor, finally stops being theory and becomes steel under your boots. The place is built for him: towers of gutted hulls wired into a single nervous system of chained drones, jury-rigged turrets, and cutter arms that only someone who lived their life in maintenance bays could truly command. From here he can vanish cargo, erase sensor echoes, and, if given a little more time, turn the surrounding trade lanes into a minefield of weaponized debris no traffic controller could ever untangle. The trail from that drifting tug in orbit to the grease-stained garage pointed the same way each time, through altered firmware and TS-? signatures, through dockside whispers about ghost salvage and workers getting quiet help from an unseen hand.
zh: 这座被遗忘的火卫二废料场，是每一笔失踪货运、每一则幽灵货船传闻终于不再是理论、而变成你靴下钢铁的地方。这地方是为他造的：一座座被掏空的船壳塔，接进由串联无人机、临时拼凑炮塔与切割臂构成的单一神经系统——只有一生都在维修舱里度过的人才真正指挥得动。从这里，他能让货物消失、抹掉传感器回声，若再多给一点时间，还能把周围的贸易航道变成一片交通控制员永远解不开的武器化残骸雷场。从轨道上那艘漂移拖船到那间油污斑斑的车库，线索每次都指向同一方向——穿过被改动的固件与 TS-? 签名，穿过码头边关于幽灵打捞与工人得到无形之手暗中帮助的低语。

#en: The Deserted Relay Station hangs in the dark like a forgotten nerve in a severed limb, still wired into the same grav-lane mesh Vector has been twisting for years. Its dishes are old enough to be ignored by modern traffic audits, yet vital enough that any signal pushed through here ripples across half a sector. This is where he has nested his final experiment, feeding stolen buoy keys and corrupted drift tables into a spine nobody bothered to decommission, preparing to bend routes until another convoy dies the way the first one did. Too many captains, too many clerks, saw the anomalies and filed them away as glitches. All I have so far are a burned buoy core in high orbit, packet ghosts from an abandoned listening post, and the same signature threaded through both, repeating like a warning nobody wanted to hear.
zh: 那座"被遗弃的中继站"像断肢上一根被遗忘的神经悬在黑暗中，仍接在"向量"多年来一直在扭动的同一张引力通道网上。它的天线盘老旧到足以被现代交通审计忽略，却又重要到任何从这里推送出去的信号都会在半个星区激起涟漪。这里就是他安放最后实验的地方：把偷来的浮标密钥与损坏的漂移表喂进一根没人费心退役的脊柱，准备掰弯航线，直到又一支车队像第一支那样死去。太多船长、太多文书看见了那些异常，却把它们当作小故障归档了事。目前为止，我只有高轨道上一枚烧毁的浮标核心、一座废弃听音哨发出的封包幽灵，以及贯穿两者的同一签名，反复着像一则没人想听的警告。

#en: The sealed monitoring pod sits deep under rock and old fear, a place built for people who watch patterns for a living and then pretend nothing is wrong. Down here, the air tastes of stale power and rerouted protocols, all those quiet updates and altered schedules that slipped in over years while no one with rank bothered to ask why. Whatever is buried in these records is where the cartographer first brushed up against someone the UC was not supposed to be running, and where their routines began to bend together.  \n\nSo far, the trail goes from a forgotten cache in the back end of nowhere to this analyst's hideaway full of half-erased telemetry, and now to a classified file that mentions the same name and an unnamed companion in the same breath, just before ship movements started to drift off their expected lines.
zh: 那座密封监控舱深埋在岩石与旧日的恐惧之下，一个为那些以观察模式为生、然后又假装一切无事的人而建的地方。在这下面，空气尝起来像陈旧的电力与被改道的协议，所有那些多年来溜进来的安静更新与改动日程，而没有一个有官阶的人费心问过为什么。埋在这些记录里的，是那位制图师第一次撞上某个联殖本不该在运作的人的地方，也是他们的例程开始彼此弯折的地方。  \n\n目前为止，这条线索从天涯之外一处被遗忘的储藏点，到这个塞满半擦除遥测的分析员藏身处，如今又到一份机密文件——它把同一个名字与一个无名同伴放在同一个呼吸里提起，就在船只活动开始偏离预期航线之前不久。

#en: Whatever the truth of the story, this is where it started to grow legs. The old recon hide still squats above a dead valley, half its arrays stripped, but the hardened recorders inside were built to see what no one was supposed to talk about. UC overwatch once watched this region for smugglers and deserters; now the only thing worth trusting is what those lenses caught when a certain navigator slipped their net. If there is any unedited glimpse of how he moves through the dark, it will be buried in this bunker. So far the trail runs from a forgotten rock with a corrupted slate, to falsified cargo logs on a wandering freighter, to war-era simulations that do not match their own summaries and every retelling in bars and briefing rooms points back to one quiet mathematician whose paths keep intersecting missing ships.
zh: 无论这故事真相如何，这里正是它开始长出腿的地方。那座旧侦察掩体仍蹲在一道死谷上方，半数阵列被剥走，可里面加固的记录仪本就是为记录没人该谈论的东西而造。联殖监视队曾在此注视走私者与逃兵；如今唯一值得信任的，是当某位领航员溜过他们的网时那些镜片捕捉到的东西。若说关于他如何在黑暗中移动还有任何未经剪辑的一瞥，它就会埋在这座掩体里。目前为止，线索从一块带着损坏数据板的被遗忘岩石，到一艘漂游货船上被伪造的货运日志，再到与自身摘要都不符的战时模拟，而酒吧与简报室里的每一次重述都指回一名安静的数学家——他的路径不断与失踪的船只相交。
